Dear [Respondent's Name],

We are writing to formally demand that you immediately cease and desist from infringing upon our intellectual property rights. Specifically, we are concerned about your use of the trade mark in question, which has been established as our registered trade mark under the Trade Marks Act 1995 (Cth).

The relevant period for the purposes of s 92(4)(b) is from 29 December 2000 to 29 December 2003. During this period, Pioneer Computers filed non-use applications against you. As per s 101 of the Act, if the grounds for the application are established and the proceedings have not been discontinued or dismissed, the Registrar may decide to remove the trade mark from the Register in respect of the goods and/or services to which the application relates.

In the case of Pioneer Computers, the Registrar determined that the term "computer peripheral devices" includes DVD-ROMs and DVD writers, among other items. Pioneer Computers provided evidence of use of the Pioneer KK marks on these items within the relevant period. However, you have failed to demonstrate use of the Pioneer KK marks on the entirety of goods known as computer peripherals and on the removal services within the relevant period.

We request that you immediately cease using the Pioneer KK trade mark in connection with the goods and services listed in the non-use applications. Failure to comply with this demand will leave us no choice but to take further legal action to protect our intellectual property rights.

We hope to resolve this matter amicably and without the need for further legal proceedings. Please confirm in writing that you will cease all infringing activities immediately.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]
[Your Position]
[Your Contact Information]
